Samir - great questions. Quick answers at a high level (we'll go deeper in the tech call):

Isolation model
- Dedicated: we allocate a dedicated GPU pool to your account (no other tenants scheduled on the same physical hosts). That provides the strongest isolation and predictable tail latency.
- Shared (hosted): multi-tenant scheduler with continuous batching and affinity controls; we mitigate noisy-neighbor with tenant throttles and prefix/KV caching, but it is still shared hardware.
- Private VPC: combines dedicated instance reservations with customer-managed networking and KMS; best for regulated environments.

SLOs and guarantees
- We can offer SLOs in a Dedicated contract (95th and P99 targets) with SLA credits tied to missed SLOs. I attached the redwood-dedicated-slos.pdf with the standard language and remediation steps.

Bursting and autoscale
- Dedicated pools support a configurable burst policy: baseline reserved capacity + short-lived burst buffer. Burst uses either pre-provisioned spare nodes or on-demand cloud instances depending on region. We'll show cost examples in the deep-dive.

Cost model (summary)
- Committed baseline: monthly reserved capacity (predictable unit rate).
- Burst: metered overage or an on-demand per-minute rate - typically higher but only for the burst window.

Next steps
- Confirm you can do Dec 16 for a 60-90 minute technical deep-dive (solutions + infra + procurement).
- Please send an example qps/seq length distribution for your baseline and burst windows so we can size the pool.

I've attached the comparison spreadsheet and the SLO doc again for quick reference. If you want, I can also prepare two cost scenarios (committed 200 QPS vs committed 100 QPS + burst buffer) and share before the call.

Thanks,
Marissa
